name: Virgin coconut oil
short: Case report: severe gut allergy to coconut oil in baby formula. Coconut oil, type unstated: LDL up ~10 mg/dL vs other oils. Virgin: triglycerides down, HDL up; subgroup under 50: total cholesterol up.
text: The two broader meta-analyses below cover coconut oil in general, and their abstracts do not say whether the oil was virgin. A meta-analysis of 16 trial publications found that coconut oil raised LDL cholesterol by 10.47 mg/dL and HDL cholesterol by 4.00 mg/dL compared with non-tropical vegetable oils, with no significant effect on blood sugar, inflammation or body fat measures, and concluded that coconut oil results in significantly higher LDL cholesterol than these oils. A second meta-analysis found similar rises in total cholesterol (15.42 mg/dL) and LDL cholesterol (10.14 mg/dL) compared with other oils and fats, larger than with corn, palm, soybean and safflower oils but not olive oil, while LDL cholesterol was lower than with butter; its authors suggested coconut oil consumption can be one of the risk factors for cardiovascular disease in South Asians. For virgin coconut oil specifically, a meta-analysis of 14 randomised trials in 1049 adults (2 to 24 weeks) found lower triglycerides and higher HDL cholesterol with no significant change in other lipid markers, although in a subgroup analysis total cholesterol rose significantly in participants under 50; and in a 4-week randomised trial in 94 healthy adults aged 50 to 75 eating 50 g a day, LDL cholesterol changed no differently with extra virgin coconut oil than with olive oil and rose more with butter. A case report describes coconut allergy in an 8-month-old baby fed infant formulas that contained coconut as an ingredient (the abstract does not say whether it was virgin oil): the first formula caused a severe gastrointestinal disorder that disappeared on a second formula, in which the coconut had been physico-chemically modified, and a third caused a relapse; coconut was the only allergen the formulas had in common, and coconut oil was identified as the cause by re-introduction, skin and specific IgE tests. In a 2-week randomised, double-blind trial in which 34 people with mild to moderate dry skin, all with negative patch tests to the test products beforehand, applied either virgin coconut oil or mineral oil to their legs, no adverse reactions occurred during the study. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
